4131:
** πλήκ-της**, ου, ὁ,
**striker, brawler,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 19 (_plural_, see l. πρῆκται), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1221b14, NT.1Tim.3.3}}; **violent, fierce,** ἄνδρες π. καὶ μάχιμοι {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Dio” 30, compare “Phil.” 9}}; of wine, π. καὶ ὀξύς {{Refs|[prev. author] 2.132d}}; of the sun, {{Refs|[prev. work]920c, compare 653f: _superlative_ πληκτίστατος 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1441.26, “Etymologicum Magnum” 31.16.}}
4143:
** πλοῖον**, τό,
(πλέω) properly **floating vessel**: hence, generally, **ship,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 602, “Ag.” 625, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.168, “IG” 12.128.5, etc.: more nearly defined, π. λεπτά}} small **craft,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.36, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.83}}; π. ἁλιευτικόν a fishing-**boat,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.20}}; ἱππαγωγὰ π. **transports** for horses, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.48}}; π. μακρά **ships** of war, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] 5.30, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.14}}; π. στρογγύλα or φορτηγικά **ships** of burden, merchantmen, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.21; μεγάλα π. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.78; ἱερὸν π. τοῦ Ὀσείριος “OGI” 56.51 (Canopus, 3rd c.BC): when distinguished from ναῦς}} without _adjective_, mostly **merchant-ship** or **transport,** as opposed to ship of war, τοῖς π. καὶ ταῖς ναυσί {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.116, compare 6.44}}; πλεῖν μὴ μακρᾷ νηΐ, ἄλλῳ δὲ κωπήρει πλοίῳ Foed.{{Refs 5th c.BC+|cited in [same work] 4.118; πλοῖά τε καὶ τριήρεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 295d}}; πλοῖα alone, ={τριήρεις}, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.1, Docum. cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.106.}}
4148:
** πλουτ-ίζω**,
_Attic dialect_ _future_ **-ιῶ**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Timocles Comicus 4.8}}:— **make wealthy, enrich,** τινα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 586, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.22; ἀρετῇ τινας [prev. author] “Mem.” 4.2.9; τὴν πατρίδα “IGRom.” 3.199 (from Ancyra): iron., π. τινὰ ἄτης (ἄτην codices) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1268}}:—_passive_, Ἅιδης στεναγμοῖς καὶ γόοις π. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 30; τούτοις π. ὑπὸ σοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.27}}; ἀπὸ βοσκημάτων, ἐκ τῆς πόλεως, **gain one's wealth** from.., {{Refs|[prev. author] “Mem.” 2.1.28, “Vect.” 4.14.}}
4150:
** πλύνω** [ῡ],
_Epic dialect_ _imperfect_ πλύνεσκον {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.155}}: _future_ πλῠνῶ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 248, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.11}}; _Ionic dialect_ and _Epic dialect_ πλῠνέω {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.31, 59:}}_aorist_ ἔπλῡνα, _Epic dialect_ πλῦνα {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.93, (ἐκ-, περι-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1062, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.9}}:—_middle_, _future_ πλῠνοῦμαι {{LXX+5th c.BC+|LXX.Num.31.24 (ἐκ-πλυνεῖται in _passive_ sense, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1064)}}: _aorist_ _participle_ πλυνάμενος {{LXX+5th c.BC+|LXX.Lev.13.6, (ἐκ-) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.73}}:—_passive_, _future_ πλῠθήσομαι (πλυνθ- {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus) “Comica Adespota” 715}}: _aorist_ ἐπλύθην [ῠ], _3rd.pers._ _singular_ _subjunctive_ πλυθῇ {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.15.4}}; _participle_ πλυθέν {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.76.18, πλυθείσης 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Vita Pythagorae - Porphyrii Opuscula” 34}}: _perfect_ πέπλῠμαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.(Sp.”) 65, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.150, (κατα-) 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.178}}; _participle_ πεπλυμένος {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PCair.Zen.” 92 (3rd c.BC)}}:—**wash, clean,** properly of linen. clothes, etc. (opposed to λούομαι **bathe,** νίζω **wash the hands** or **feet**), εἵματα πλύνεσκον {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.155; ἴομεν πλυνέουσαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.31}}; πλῦνάν τε (i.e. εἵματα) κάθηράν τε ῥύπα πάντα{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. work] 93; π. κῴδια 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 166; τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ἱμάτιον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 161e; τὰς κοιλίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 160; ἄμμον 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Lapidibus” 58; ἐάν τις ἢ λόηται ἢ πλύνει τι ἐν ταῖς κρήναις “IG” 12(5).569.5 (Ceos, 3rd c.BC)}}; στολήν {{LXX|LXX.Gen.49.11}}:—_passive_, σησάμου πεπλυμένου {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PCair.Zen.” 562.19 (3rd c.BC)}}; σκίλλης πλυθείσης Porph. [prev. cited]
**b** _metaphorically_, πέπλυται τὸ πρᾶγμα the thing **is washed to pieces,** i. e. **worn out,** {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC(?): Sosipater Comicus 1.3: hence τὸ πεπατημένον καὶ πεπλυμένον}}**threadbare, hackneyed,** {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor “Ars Rhetorica” p.190H.}}
**II** as a slang term, πλύνειν τινά '**give** him **a dressing', abuse,** κἀκυκλοβόρει κἄπλυνε {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 381; ἀλλήλους πλυνοῦμεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.11; πλύνοντες αὑτοὺς τἀπόρρητα [prev. author] 58.40; τὸν πατέρα καὶ σὲ τούς τε σοὺς ἐγὼ πλυνῶ 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 608; τοὺς κρείσσονας 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 46.4: with _dative_ modi, τὸν τάριχον τουτονὶ πλύνων ἅπασιν ὅσα σύνοιδ᾽ αὐτῷ κακά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 200: with double_accusative_, πλυνεῖ τε τὰ κακὰ τῶν κακῶν ὑμᾶς 5th c.BC: Diocles Comicus 2. (πλῠ-ν-yω _cognate_ with πλε (ϝ) -ω}} also with Lithuanian _pláuti_ 'bathe', OSlavonic _pluti_ 'flow', 'sail'.)
4173:
** πολῑτάρχ-ης**, ου, ὁ,
**civic magistrate,** at Thessalonica, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|NT.Act.17.6; at Lete, “SIG” 700.2 (2nd c.BC)}}; in Egypt, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“POxy.” 745.4 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD)}}:—also **πολῑταρχ-ος**, ὁ, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 26.12.}}
4179:
** πολλαπλᾰσί-ων**, ον,
_genitive_ ονος, ={πολλαπλάσιος}, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“Num.Chron.” 1905.114 (Abonuteichos, 2nd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 35.4.4, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.215b: with _genitive_, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 9}}. _adverb_ **-όνως**{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.164.}}
4180:
** πολυ-λογία**, ἡ,
**loquacity, much to say,** {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 641e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.3, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1295a2, LXX.Pro.10.19, etc.}}
4193: **from Pontus, Pontic **, {{8th/7th c.BC|Iliad by Homer}} δένδρεον, probably, **the bird-cherry **, {{Refs 5th c.BC|Herdotus Historicus}} (Middle Liddel)
